transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been having some really troubling thoughts lately that I can't get out of my head. It feels like people are constantly watching me and monitoring everything I do, and I don't know who to trust anymore.
Besides these thoughts, have you been experiencing any significant changes in your mood, such as periods of feeling extremely low or unusually high and energetic?

Yes, for about the past month, I've been feeling extremely low, sad, and empty, with no motivation or interest in doing anything. I also feel constantly tired and exhausted all the time. But I have definitely never had any periods of feeling unusually high, hyper, or energetic.
Have you experienced these paranoid thoughts even during times when your mood was relatively stable, or do they only occur when you are feeling at your lowest?

Yes, I've definitely experienced them even when my mood was relatively stable. There was a period of about two weeks where I felt okay and wasn't feeling so down, but I still felt like I was being watched and targeted. Those thoughts seem to persist even when I'm not feeling depressed.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports that the psychotic symptoms (paranoid ideation) persist during periods of mood stability, which effectively rules out Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features, as the latter requires psychotic symptoms to occur exclusively during a major depressive episode. Therefore, Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) remains the primary candidate.
